proofs.proof_tex:
Under \(\texttt{ass:one-unsupported-row}\) and
\(\texttt{ass:binary-free-row}\), the generalized unsupported-row objects
specialize to
\[
 \mathcal R_{\mathrm{free}}=\{rstar\},
 \qquad
 \mathcal P_{\mathrm{free}}
 =\{(1-q,q):0\leq q\leq1\}.
\]
After separating the three fully Markovian restrictions, the corrected
\(\texttt{def:model-class}\) and
\(\texttt{def:finite-unsupported-model-class}\) impose the same membership
conditions in this specialization: they use the same finite schema and graph,
induce the same source and target groundings, require mutual independence of
distinct exogenous variables, forbid exogenous relational parents, forbid a
non-relational exogenous parent from being shared by distinct ground endogenous
variables, share finite mechanisms by type--context key, reproduce \(Psrc\), and
use \(K\) at every target-relevant key having positive source support.  The
unique unrestricted target-relevant key is \(rstar\), and its row is
\((1-q,q)\).  Hence
\[
 \mathcal M_{\mathrm{fin}}=Mone,
 \qquad Q_{\mathrm{fin}}=Q.
\]
Replaying \(\texttt{def:multivariate-target-polynomial}\) at
\(p_{rstar}=(1-q,q)\) is precisely the replay defining \(F\).  Equivalently,
this equality is the one established by
\(\texttt{lem:polynomial-reduction}\):
\[
 \Phi\bigl((1-q,q)\bigr)=F(q),
 \qquad 0\leq q\leq1.
\]
The specialization of
\(\texttt{thm:sharp-finite-unsupported-rows}\) therefore gives
\[
 \Theta=F([0,1])
 =\left[\min_{q\in[0,1]}F(q),
         \max_{q\in[0,1]}F(q)\right].
\]
In particular, the reverse inclusion is witnessed by compatible finite-noise,
type-shared RSCMs and is not merely an outer bound.

It remains to identify these extrema with \(L\) and \(U\).  Suppose first that
\(F\) is nonconstant, and let \(c\in(0,1)\) be a minimizer.  For every
sufficiently small \(h>0\),
\[
 \frac{F(c+h)-F(c)}{h}\geq0,
 \qquad
 \frac{F(c)-F(c-h)}{h}\leq0.
\]
Both quotients converge to \(F'(c)\), because a polynomial is differentiable.
Thus \(F'(c)\geq0\) and \(F'(c)\leq0\), whence \(F'(c)=0\).  Reversing the two
inequalities gives the same conclusion for an interior maximizer.  Therefore
every optimizer is either \(0\), \(1\), or a feasible distinct real root of
\(F'\), and so belongs to \(Ccrit\) by
\(\texttt{def:critical-candidates}\).  Since \(Ccrit\subseteq[0,1]\), while
all global optimizers belong to \(Ccrit\),
\[
 \min_{q\in[0,1]}F(q)=\min_{c\in Ccrit}F(c)=L,
 \qquad
 \max_{q\in[0,1]}F(q)=\max_{c\in Ccrit}F(c)=U.
\]
If \(F\) is constant, \(F(Ccrit)\) is a singleton and \(0,1\in Ccrit\), so
the same equalities hold.  This proves, without any comparator-domain
assumption,
\[
 \Theta=F([0,1])=[L,U].
\]

We now prove the conditional comparator clauses.  Let \(\mathcal E_{\rho}\)
denote the Ejaz--Bareinboim Definition~3.2 anchor class for the fixed causal
problem, let \(\mathcal D_5\) denote the domain satisfying their separately
stated Section~5 assumptions~(I)--(III), and put
\[
 \mathcal E_5=\mathcal E_{\rho}\cap\mathcal D_5.
\]
By the corrected
\(\texttt{lem:ejaz-bareinboim-rho-markovian-scope}\), Definition~3.2 forbids
an exogenous relational parent and allows a non-relational exogenous parent to
be shared only by attributes of the same instance.  The corresponding
restrictions are explicit in the corrected definition of \(Mone\).  The
Section~5 domain has additional requirements, including one uniform finite
bound on relational-parent multiset size over every skeleton in its declared
domain.  The maximum over the finitely many groundings listed in \(Rsrc\) and
\(\rho\) proves only a bound for that finite list; it does not prove a bound
over every admissible skeleton.  Consequently no inclusion of \(Mone\) in
\(\mathcal E_5\) is inferred here.

Assume the inclusion appearing explicitly in the theorem's comparator clause,
\(Mone\subseteq\mathcal E_5\), and suppose that \(F\) is nonconstant.  Then
there are \(q_1,q_2\in[0,1]\) with \(F(q_1)\neq F(q_2)\).  The structural
sharpness equality already proved supplies \(M_1,M_2\in Mone\) such that
\[
 Q(M_1)=F(q_1)\neq F(q_2)=Q(M_2).
\]
The assumed inclusion puts both witnesses in \(\mathcal E_5\).  Hence the
query is not point identified on \(\mathcal E_5\); by inclusion, it is also
not point identified on any structural superclass containing
\(\mathcal E_5\).  Theorem~5.2 and Corollary~D.7 from the cited comparator
lemma are invoked only on \(\mathcal E_5\), not outside it.  A return value
\(\mathsf{FAIL}\) there cannot change the already proved equality
\(\Theta=[L,U]\) for \(Mone\).  Conversely, inclusion alone supplies no bound
on the query values of models in a strict superclass, so it does not establish
that \([L,U]\) is sharp for that superclass.

If \(F\) is constant, the structural equality gives \(L=U\) on \(Mone\).
When the comparator-compatible class equals \(Mone\), substitution of equal
sets transfers this singleton.  Under strict containment, constancy on the
subset \(Mone\) imposes no restriction on query values at the additional
models.  Thus neither singleton identification nor sharpness transfers from
\(Mone\) to a strict comparator superclass.

Finally, unsupportedness alone does not force \(\mathsf{FAIL}\).  Consider a
finite acyclic target having two binary nodes \(A\) and \(X\) in distinct
instances and no endogenous edges.  Let the supported row of \(A\) be fair,
let the unsupported row of \(X\) have success probability \(q\), and take
\(B=\{A=X\}\).  The ground noises are independent, there is no exogenous
relational parent, and no permitted within-instance sharing connects these
distinct instances.  Direct truncated factorization gives
\[
 P(B\mid\operatorname{do}(a))
 =(1-q)\frac12+q\frac12=\frac12.
\]
The relational-parent multiset bound for the declared domain of this example
is zero, so the example lies in \(\mathcal E_5\); completeness in the cited
comparator lemma therefore precludes \(\mathsf{FAIL}\) for this identified
query.  The unsupported row is nevertheless present in the target
factorization, and its cancellation proves that unsupported status alone does
not imply failure.

The smallest repeated-row check also shows that type sharing is load bearing.
With two independent target nodes using the same unsupported binary key and
with the event of exactly one success, the shared-row map is
\[
 q(1-q)+(1-q)q=2q(1-q)\leq\frac12.
\]
If type sharing alone is removed, occurrence-specific rows \(q_1=1\) and
\(q_2=0\) make the same event have probability one.  Thus the common
coordinate \(q\), and hence the claimed image \(F([0,1])\), genuinely depends
on the type-sharing condition.

proposed_statement_changes.reason: The structural sharp-set equality is unchanged. The comparator clauses are narrowed to the explicit intersection of the Definition~3.2 anchor and the Section~5 domain, and upward transfer now requires the stated inclusion of \(Mone\) in that intersection.

proposed_assumptions.condition:
No ground endogenous variable in an admissible source or target grounding has
an exogenous relational parent.
proposed_assumptions.reason: This is the correctly directed graphical restriction from the published Markovian anchor and is not implied by mutual independence of distinct exogenous variables.

proposed_assumptions.condition:
No non-relational exogenous variable in an admissible source or target
grounding is a parent of two distinct ground endogenous variables.
proposed_assumptions.reason: The fully Markovian structural class excludes shared non-relational exogenous parents, a restriction distinct from independence of different exogenous variables and standard in the cited Markovian formulation.

proposed_assumptions.condition:
There exists one finite integer bound such that, for every skeleton over \(S\)
and \(G\) in the declared Ejaz--Bareinboim comparator domain of interest and
every ground endogenous variable in that skeleton, the cardinality of its
instantiated relational-parent multiset is at most that bound.
proposed_assumptions.reason: This is a standard comparator-only Section~5 condition over every skeleton in the declared domain of interest. It is not inferred from the finite list of source and target groundings and is not added to either structural model class.

proposed.condition:
All distinct exogenous variables occurring in the admissible source and target
groundings are mutually independent.

proposed_core_edits.reason: Mutual independence is stated as a condition on distinct exogenous variables; it does not silently stand in for either of the separate graphical parent restrictions.

proposed.name: One-unseen-row compatible RSCM class
proposed.construction:
\(Mone=\{M: M\text{ is a finite RSCM over }S\text{ and }G;\ M\text{ induces
the source groundings }Rsrc\text{ and target grounding }\rho\text{ encoded by
}Ictx;\text{ all distinct exogenous variables are mutually independent; no
ground endogenous variable has an exogenous relational parent; no
non-relational exogenous variable is a parent of two distinct ground endogenous
variables; mechanisms are shared by type--context key; }M\text{ reproduces
}Psrc;\ M\text{ uses the rows }K\text{ recovered from positive-probability
source parent contexts; and }M\text{ has exactly one unrestricted
target-relevant binary row at }rstar\}\).

proposed_core_edits.reason: The replacement preserves the intended fully Markovian class while making independence and the two graphical parent restrictions explicit. The comparator-only global parent-multiset bound is not added.

proposed.name: Finite-unsupported-row compatible RSCM class
proposed.construction:
\(\mathcal M_{\mathrm{fin}}\) is the class of finite RSCMs over \(S\) and
\(G\) that induce the source groundings \(Rsrc\) and target grounding
\(\rho\) encoded by \(Ictx\), have mutually independent distinct exogenous
variables, have no ground endogenous variable with an exogenous relational
parent, have no non-relational exogenous variable that is a parent of two
distinct ground endogenous variables, have type-shared finite mechanisms,
reproduce \(Psrc\), use the recovered rows \(K\) at every target-relevant
positive-source-support key, and leave precisely the target-relevant keys in
\(\mathcal R_{\mathrm{free}}\) unrestricted over their native finite outcome
alphabets.

proposed_core_edits.reason: The generalized class receives exactly the same explicit fully Markovian restrictions as the one-row class and remains independent of the comparator-only global bound.

proposed.comparator_claim: Canonical finite SCMs reduce arbitrary discrete counterfactual sharp bounds to a polynomial program.
Polynomial programming yields numerical sharp or epsilon-sharp bounds and confidence-region relaxations for discrete causal queries.
Untrusted algebraic root certificates can be checked skeptically by verified univariate CAD and Sturm--Tarski computations.
Root counting and interval subdivision decide univariate polynomial relation systems soundly and completely in PVS.
Exact real-root isolation with multiplicities and nonsquare-free inputs has explicit polynomial bit-complexity bounds.
Unnested univariate parametric Markov-chain model checking is polynomial-time after the parametric model is explicit.
A response-signature LP gives tight causal-order bounds and constructs attaining SCMs.

prose_updates.tldr: For any finite family of target-relevant unsupported finite-categorical shared rows, the fully Markovian relational causal set is exactly the compact interval obtained as the image of an explicit rational polynomial over the product of row simplices, with finite-noise endpoint witnesses. The one unsupported binary row remains the tractable specialization with exact algebraic certificates. Here fully Markovian means mutually independent distinct exogenous variables, no exogenous relational parents, and no non-relational exogenous parent shared by distinct ground endogenous variables. Comparison with Ejaz--Bareinboim is only on the intersection of their Definition~3.2 \(\rho\)-Markovian anchor and their Section~5 assumptions~(I)--(III); the global parent-multiset bound is not inferred from the finitely listed groundings. Nonconstant \(F\) transfers nonidentification only when inclusion in that intersection is explicit, and neither the sharp interval nor a singleton transfers to a strict superclass. Supported-row boxes use \(\delta_{\times}=1-\prod_r(1-\epsilon_r)^{m_r}\), while the frozen exhaustive-assignment grammar, rather than relational treewidth itself, accounts for the \(2^k\) incidence witness.

project_justification.gap: Complete relational identification on the published Definition~3.2 and Section~5 intersection does not return the exact compatible causal range after nonidentification. Generic polynomial bounds also do not realize every product-simplex point by a type-shared fully Markovian RSCM or certify the relational derivation and endpoint models.
project_justification.niche: Finitely many unsupported finite-categorical rows admit an exact structural reduction on a fully Markovian no-shared-parent class; the one-binary-row specialization additionally admits efficient exact univariate algebraic certification.
project_justification.fill: The project proves the multivariate structural sharp image and finite-noise endpoint witnesses without a global skeleton-degree assumption, supplies a skeptical univariate certificate, and states published-comparator consequences only on the explicit Definition~3.2 and Section~5 intersection.

prose_updates.related_work: Ejaz and Bareinboim's Definition~3.2 gives the \(\rho\)-Markovian anchor: it excludes exogenous relational parents and allows a shared non-relational exogenous parent only for attributes of the same instance. Their Section~5 completeness and neural results apply separately under assumptions~(I)--(III), including finite observed domains and one uniform relational-parent-multiset bound over every skeleton in the declared domain; Appendix~D, Corollary~D.7 is the version-two neural correctness result. The present exact image is proved for a fully Markovian subclass with mutually independent distinct exogenous variables and no shared non-relational exogenous parent, without assuming that global bound. Consequently, comparison is restricted to the intersection with the published Section~5 domain. A nonconstant image proves nonidentification upward only when the fully Markovian compatible class is explicitly included in that intersection; neither its sharp interval nor a constant-polynomial singleton transfers to a strict superclass. Zhang, Tian, and Bareinboim provide canonical finite-SCM polynomial programs, and Duarte et al. provide general numerical polynomial bounds and confidence-constraint relaxations; neither supplies this relational product-simplex realization theorem, exact univariate relational certificate, or multiplicative labeled-occurrence enclosure. Li, Passmore, and Paulson, Narkawicz, Mu\~noz, and Dutle, and Tsigaridas and Emiris supply the skeptical algebraic and root-isolation substrate. Hutschenreiter, Baier, and Klein identify a polynomial explicit-univariate model-checking core. Rossetto and Antonucci construct attaining models for order-based nonrelational bounds, but their witnesses do not impose the present type-shared fully Markovian semantics.
prose_updates.honest_scope: Structural soundness, compact interval form, endpoint attainment, and the finite breakpoint atom-count bound are proved for any finite family of unsupported finite-categorical rows in fully observed, acyclic, type-shared RSCMs with mutually independent distinct exogenous variables, no exogenous relational parents, and no non-relational exogenous parent shared by distinct ground endogenous variables. These structural results do not assume a global bound on relational-parent multiset size. That bound is a comparator-only condition in the Ejaz--Bareinboim Section~5 domain and cannot be inferred from the finite source and target groundings. All procedure and neural-completeness comparisons are restricted to the intersection of that domain with the Definition~3.2 anchor; nonidentification transfers only under explicit class inclusion, and sharp ranges or singleton identification transfer only under class equality. Exact derivative-root optimization, algebraic endpoint comparison, polynomial-size certificates, the sharp optimizer-degree guarantee, and the at-most-two algebraic-noise-mass guarantee remain specific to one unsupported binary row. Efficient exact multivariate optimization, compact circuit-level incidence, conditional postintervention queries, exact nuisance-box projection, and empirical usefulness beyond the documented N3 example remain open. The sampling enclosure is conservative and uses \(\delta_{\times}\leq\min\{1,\sum_r m_r\epsilon_r\}\).
